methods.label: Complete the square and eliminate the parameter
methods.explanation:
Completing the square reveals the vertex directly. Since \(a>0\),
\[
y=a\left(x+\frac{t}{2a}\right)^2+c-\frac{t^2}{4a},
\]
and the squared term is smallest when \(x=-t/(2a)\). Thus
\[
x_t=-\frac{t}{2a},\qquad y_t=c-\frac{t^2}{4a}.
\]

Write a vertex as \((X,Y)\). The first coordinate gives \(t=-2aX\); substituting into the second gives
\[
Y=c-\frac{(-2aX)^2}{4a}=c-aX^2.
\]
Because \(-a\ne0\), this is a downward-opening parabola.

We must also check that every point on this parabola occurs. For any real \(X\), choosing the real parameter \(t=-2aX\) produces the vertex \((X,c-aX^2)\). Therefore the locus is the whole parabola, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
methods.levelReason: Completing the square, substitution, and recognition of a quadratic graph are school algebra; no calculus is needed.
